ei.title: Practice 01 — 윤리적 기준이 소비자들의 소비성향에 미치는 영향
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본2

fullPassage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively (A)[homogeneous / distinctive]. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were (B)[willing / hesitant] to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in (C)[shaping / analyzing] those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) homogeneous=동질적인, (B) willing=기꺼이 ~하는, (C) shaping=형성하는
det.analysis:
✅ ① homogeneous — willing — shaping: 원문 일치. 동질 제품 전제 + 프리미엄 지불 의향 + 결과 형성 맥락
❌ ② distinctive — willing — shaping: (A) distinctive(구별되는)는 homogeneous(동질적인)의 반의어로 실험 전제 왜곡
❌ ③ homogeneous — hesitant — shaping: (B) hesitant(망설이는)는 willing(기꺼이)의 반의어로 소비자 행동 왜곡
❌ ④ homogeneous — willing — analyzing: (C) analyzing(분석하는)은 shaping(형성하는)과 의미 대립
det.tip: homogeneous(동질적인) / willing to pay(기꺼이 지불) / shaping results(결과를 형성) — 세 단어 모두 본문 핵심

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers (A)[conducted / ignored] a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight (B)[premium / surcharge] for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep (C)[discount / markup]. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) conducted=실시했다, (B) premium=할증료/웃돈, (C) discount=할인
det.analysis:
❌ ① ignored — premium — discount: (A) ignored(무시했다)는 conducted(실시했다)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ④ conducted — premium — discount: 원문 일치. 실험 실시 + 윤리 제품에 웃돈 지불 + 비윤리 제품 할인 구매
❌ ③ conducted — surcharge — discount: (B) surcharge(할증료)는 premium(할증료)과 의미 유사하나 본문의 premium 단어 사용
❌ ② conducted — premium — markup: (C) markup(인상)은 discount(할인)의 반의어로 부적절
det.tip: conducted experiments(실험 실시) / slight premium(약간의 웃돈) / steep discount(큰 할인) — 실험 결과의 핵심 구조

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that (A)[low / high] standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a (B)[steep / gentle] discount. What's more, consumer (C)[attitudes / indifference] played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) low=낮은(비윤리 기준), (B) steep=가파른/큰, (C) attitudes=태도
det.analysis:
❌ ① high — gentle — attitudes: (A) high(높은)는 비윤리적 기준 집단이 아니고, (B) gentle(온순한)는 steep(가파른)과 반대 의미
❌ ② low — mild — attitudes: (B) mild(약한)는 steep(큰)의 반의어로 할인 정도를 축소시켜 부적절
✅ ③ low — steep — attitudes: 원문 일치. 낮은 기준 집단 + 큰 폭 할인 + 소비자 태도가 결과에 영향
❌ ④ low — steep — indifference: (C) indifference(무관심)는 attitudes(태도)와 의미 대립
det.tip: low standards(낮은 기준) / steep discount(큰 할인) / consumer attitudes(소비자 태도) — 실험 결과의 핵심 세 요소

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for ①<u>unethical</u> companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using ②<u>high</u> ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a ③<u>steep</u> discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior ④<u>rewarded</u> the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 소비자가 더 많이 지불하는 대상은 '윤리적' 기업 제품. unethical(비윤리적)은 문맥 부적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① unethical — 원문은 good(좋은/윤리적인). 더 많이 지불하는 대상이 비윤리적 기업이라고 하면 문맥 역전
❌ ② high — 원문 일치. 높은 윤리 기준으로 만든 제품 집단 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ steep — 원문 일치. 비윤리적 제품에 큰 폭 할인을 요구한다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ rewarded — 원문 일치. 윤리적 기업에 더 높은 웃돈으로 보상한다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: consumers pay MORE for GOOD companies' products — good(좋은)을 unethical(비윤리적)로 바꾸면 전체 논리 역전

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a ①<u>series</u> of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were ②<u>willing</u> to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with ③<u>bigger</u> premiums and ④<u>rewarded</u> the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 비윤리적 기업은 '처벌'받는 것이 맞음. rewarded(보상받다)는 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① series — 원문 일치. 일련의 실험이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② willing — 원문 일치. 기꺼이 웃돈을 낸다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ bigger — 원문 일치. 더 큰 웃돈으로 보상한다는 맥락에 적절
✅ ④ rewarded — 원문은 punished(처벌했다). 비윤리 기업을 더 큰 할인으로 처벌하는 맥락에 rewarded(보상)는 부적절
det.tip: rewarded ethical companies / punished unethical ones — 대조 구조. rewarded를 punished 자리에 쓰면 논리 역전

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the ②<u>same</u> products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical ③<u>standards</u> and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight ④<u>premium</u> for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a ①<u>minor</u> part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 소비자 태도가 결과에 '큰' 역할을 했다는 것이 맞음. minor(작은)는 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ④ same — 원문 일치. 실험에서 동일한 제품을 보여주는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② standards — 원문 일치. 윤리 기준이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ premium — 원문 일치. 윤리 제품에 웃돈을 지불하는 맥락에 적절
✅ ① minor — 원문은 big(큰). 소비자 태도가 결과 형성에 큰 역할을 한다는 맥락에 minor(작은)는 부적절
det.tip: played a BIG part = 큰 역할을 하다. minor(작은)로 바꾸면 소비자 태도의 영향력을 축소시켜 본문 취지 왜곡

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A __________ group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정보를 받지 않은 집단 → A control group(통제 집단)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ control — 통제. A control group got no information으로 명시됨. 정보 없는 표준 집단
❌ ① ethical — 윤리적. 정보 없는 집단은 윤리 정보가 아님
❌ ② homogeneous — 동질적인. 제품의 특성이지 집단 구분이 아님
❌ ④ premium — 할증. 가격 개념이지 집단 특성이 아님
det.tip: A control group = 통제 집단 (정보 제공 없는 표준 비교 집단)

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made __________. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 윤리적으로 만든 제품 = ethically made _____ → goods(제품)
det.analysis:
✅ ② goods — 제품/상품. consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods
❌ ① tests — 테스트. 제품과 무관
❌ ③ results — 결과. 윤리 기준으로 만든 것은 결과가 아닌 제품
❌ ④ experiments — 실험. 제품이 아닌 연구 과정
det.tip: ethically made goods = 윤리적으로 만든 제품. premium을 지불하는 대상

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one __________ the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 또 다른 _____ 에게는 낮은 기준으로 만든 제품이라고 말함 → group(집단)
det.analysis:
❌ ③ tests — 테스트. 참여자 집단이 아님
❌ ② behavior — 행동. 제품 정보를 받은 대상이 아님
✅ ① group — 집단. another group that low standards had been used(낮은 기준이라고 들은 또 다른 집단)
❌ ④ premiums — 할증료. 웃돈이 아닌 정보를 받은 참여자 집단
det.tip: one group / another group / A control group — 세 가지 실험 참여 집단 구분

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 homogeneous와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: homogeneous=동질적인, 같은 종류의
det.analysis:
❌ ② diverse — 다양한. 반의어
✅ ③ identical — 동일한, 똑같은. 같은 종류/구성이라는 의미에서 가장 가까운 동의어
❌ ① unique — 독특한. 동질성과 반대 개념
❌ ④ superior — 우월한. 품질 비교 개념으로 동질성과 무관
det.tip: homogeneous = 동질적인 = identical(동일한) / similar(유사한). diverse(다양한)와 반대

To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in <u>shaping</u> those results. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 shaping과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: shaping=형성하는, 만들어 가는
det.analysis:
❌ ① distorting — 왜곡하는. 반대 방향의 의미
✅ ④ forming — 형성하는. shaping과 가장 가까운 동의어
❌ ③ analyzing — 분석하는. 결과를 만든다는 의미와 다름
❌ ② ignoring — 무시하는. 반대 의미
det.tip: shape results = form results = 결과를 형성하다 — distort(왜곡)과 반대

To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 rewarded와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: rewarded=보상했다, 보답했다
det.analysis:
❌ ① punished — 처벌했다. 반의어
❌ ② ignored — 무시했다. 관련 없음
❌ ③ criticized — 비판했다. 처벌과 유사하여 반의어 방향
✅ ④ compensated — 보상했다, 보답했다. rewarded와 가장 가까운 동의어
det.tip: reward = compensate = 보상하다 — punish(처벌하다)와 정반대 대조 구조

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 punished와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: punished=처벌했다 → 반의어는 보상하다
det.analysis:
❌ ① criticized — 비판했다. 처벌과 유사한 방향
✅ ③ rewarded — 보상했다. punished(처벌)의 정반대 의미. 본문에서도 대조 구조로 사용
❌ ② ignored — 무시했다. 처벌과 다른 방향이지만 반의어라 보기 어려움
❌ ④ avoided — 피했다. 처벌과 다른 개념
det.tip: rewarded ethical companies vs. punished unethical ones — 본문의 대조 구조가 반의어 관계를 명확히 보여줌

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ethically와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: ethically=윤리적으로 → 반의어는 비윤리적으로
det.analysis:
❌ ① morally — 도덕적으로. 오히려 ethically의 유의어
❌ ③ carefully — 신중하게. 윤리와 무관
✅ ② immorally — 비도덕적으로/비윤리적으로. ethically(윤리적으로)의 정반대 개념
❌ ④ cheaply — 저렴하게. 가격과 관련된 개념으로 윤리와 직접 반대 아님
det.tip: ethically(윤리적으로) ↔ immorally/unethically(비윤리적으로) — un- 접두사가 아닌 im- 단어로 대체

questions.passage:
(A) In a perfect world, consumers would <u>pay</u> more for good companies' products than unethical companies' products if the products were relatively homogeneous.

(B) Companies that invest in ethical practices find that it does <u>pay</u> off in the long run: consumers reward them with higher prices and stronger loyalty.
questions.stem: 다음 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 pay의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) pay = 지불하다, (B) pay = 이득이 되다/보람이 있다
det.analysis:
❌ ① 이득이 되다 — 지불하다: (A)(B) 의미가 반전되어 부적절
❌ ③ 보상하다 — 처벌하다: pay의 핵심 의미와 무관
✅ ② 지불하다 — 이득이 되다: (A) would pay more = 더 많이 지불하다, (B) it does pay off = 결국 이득이 된다 ←정답
❌ ④ 주의를 기울이다 — 보상하다: pay attention의 pay와 혼동 유도이나 두 문맥 모두 부적절
det.tip: pay (1) 지불하다: pay more for products (2) 이득이 되다/보람이 있다: it pays to be ethical / pay off

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "to organize and carry out a particular activity or process in a formal or systematic way"

det.korean: 정의: 특정 활동이나 과정을 공식적이고 체계적으로 조직하고 수행하다 → conduct(실시하다)
det.analysis:
❌ ④ experiment — 실험. 명사/동사지만 '조직하고 수행하다'는 행위 자체보다 대상에 가까움
❌ ② attitude — 태도. 수행 행위와 무관
✅ ① conduct — 실시하다, 수행하다. 공식적이고 체계적으로 활동을 조직하고 수행하는 행위와 정확히 일치
❌ ③ standard — 기준. 수행 행위가 아닌 평가 기준
det.tip: conduct experiments = 실험을 실시하다 — conduct a series of experiments에서 핵심 동사

questions.passage: People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and __________ (punish) the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: punish의 과거형 → punished. rewarded와 병렬 구조
det.analysis: rewarded와 접속사 and로 연결된 병렬 구조. rewarded가 과거형이므로 punish도 과거형 punished 필요
det.tip: reward — rewarded / punish — punished: 규칙 동사 -ed 과거형. and로 연결된 병렬 구조

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers __________ (conduct) a series of experiments.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: conduct의 과거형 → conducted. 과거 실험 기술
det.analysis: 실험을 실시했다는 과거 사건. To find out~으로 시작하는 과거 서술 맥락에서 conduct의 과거형 conducted 필요
det.tip: conduct — conducted: 규칙 동사 -ed 과거형. 연구자들이 실험을 실시했다(past)

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big __________ in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칙에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 소비자 태도가 결과에 큰 _____ 을 했다 → part(역할)
det.analysis:
❌ ① experiments — 실험. 태도가 실험 자체를 한 것이 아님
❌ ② goods — 제품. 태도가 형성하는 대상이지 역할이 아님
✅ ④ part — 역할. consumer attitudes played a big part(태도가 결과 형성에 큰 역할을 했다)
❌ ③ direction — 방향. 역할과는 다른 개념
det.tip: play a part in = ~에 역할을 하다. 'What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results.'

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they __________ much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 비윤리 제품 구매에서 더 극단적으로 _____ → went(나아갔다)
det.analysis:
❌ ④ conducted — 실시했다. 비윤리 제품 구매와 무관
❌ ② showed — 보여줬다. 단순 제시 개념이지 극단적 반응이 아님
❌ ① were willing — 기꺼이 했다. 웃돈 지불에만 사용되는 표현
✅ ③ went — 나아갔다. But they went much further in the other direction(그들은 반대 방향으로 더 나아갔다)
det.tip: They went much further = 더 극단적으로 나아갔다. 프리미엄 지불보다 할인 요구가 훨씬 더 컸다는 의미
